finalText:
Your Redis server at 10.0.0.12:6379 went down at 02:14:07, and the system cascaded from there.

When Redis disconnected, the cache layer fell back to direct database reads. The database got hammered immediately — every request now had to hit the store instead of being served from cache. Reads started timing out after 5 seconds, but the backlog kept growing. By 02:14:12, the queue had 52 requests piling up; by 02:31 it hit 568.

For 17 minutes, the app tried to reconnect to Redis (attempts 0 through 12, all failed). During that whole time, requests just accumulated in memory. Eventually at 02:31:44, JavaScript ran out of heap trying to hold the backlog. Worker-2 crashed, then the API went unresponsive and was killed by the supervisor.

The fix: get Redis back online at that address. After that, watch your alert thresholds — if a single cache layer goes down, you'll want to catch the cascade earlier (maybe cut requests or fail fast once queue depth hits 200–300, well before memory exhaustion).
